title: Pure greeting formatter and tests
goal: Plan a deterministic greeting formatter with unit tests, without implementing it.

tasks.description: Define the formatter contract, including input types, whitespace handling, fallback behavior, and exact output punctuation.
acceptanceCriteria: The contract specifies exact outputs for ordinary, whitespace-padded, empty, and missing names.
The contract defines handling of unsupported input types.
Any unresolved behavior is explicitly recorded before implementation.

tasks.description: Implement the pure greeting formatter according to the agreed contract using project conventions.
acceptanceCriteria: The formatter performs no I/O, modifies no external state, and does not mutate inputs.

tasks.description: Add and run unit tests for the formatter contract and deterministic behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests verify exact results for ordinary names, surrounding whitespace, blank and missing names, and Unicode names.
Tests cover unsupported input types according to the contract.
Repeated calls with the same input produce the same output.
All formatter tests pass under the project's test runner.

assumptions: The formatter accepts a name and returns a greeting string without side effects.
Proposed default behavior is to trim surrounding whitespace and return "Hello, <name>!"; missing or blank names return "Hello!".
The existing project language and test framework will be used.
questions: Should the proposed greeting text and blank-name fallback be used?
Should non-string inputs be rejected, converted, or excluded by the type contract?
